solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: She acts benevolently in good faith with merry disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the words that follow are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A kindly woman who means well and behaves cheerfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like a description of her cheerful nature but it signals rearranging GOOD FAITH and MERRY together.
explanation.definitionFit: In pantomime and fairy tales this magical figure grants wishes and helps the heroine out of pure kindness.

clue.text: Unsuccessful US agent welcomes trouble

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the agent's word holds the trouble's word inside it

parts.note: a Fed is slang for an American federal agent, as in the FBI
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: An American agent who has botched a job takes on problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that failed did not succeed, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Fine art work is attractive

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate, a piece of art

explanation.surface: A fine piece of artwork is pleasing to the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching is a slightly old-fashioned synonym for good-looking or charming.

clue.text: Distress man got in after break-up

indicators.note: to distress something is to damage or knock it about, so these letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man suffered distress after a relationship ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' reads as emotional suffering, but here it means rough treatment of the letters of MAN GOT IN AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragmentation is the process of shattering into pieces, a breaking up.

clue.text: Screen part of secret lifestyle following revolution

indicators.note: following revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
only a portion of the following words is used, the letters running across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A detail of someone's private life comes out after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Screen part' as the definition, leaving the hidden word without a signal; 'part of' is that signal, and 'Screen' alone defines. 'following revolution' turns RETLIF round.
explanation.definitionFit: A filter screens out unwanted matter, so the verb or noun senses match.

clue.text: Member of school admits always showing agitation

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the school member's word takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a school is a shoal of fish, so one member is a fish
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A pupil confesses to being permanently anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests a pupil, but it is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish activity is restless and excited, so the word describes someone visibly agitated.

clue.text: America, China and half of Russia trained Olympic athletes originally?

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America, as in USA
in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so those three letters are rearranged
the first three of the six letters in Russia are taken

explanation.surface: Athletes from three great powers trained for the Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: China means MATE through Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate); 'trained' turns RUS into URS. The question mark admits the definition is a historical fact rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The early modern Olympics were restricted to unpaid competitors, so the original athletes were non-professionals.

clue.text: Film soldiers returning to infiltrate security agency

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the soldiers' letters go inside the agency's

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: returning means the word for soldiers is read backwards

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A spy thriller in which troops come back to penetrate an intelligence service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MEN round before it is placed in the agency; 'Film' could be a verb, but here it is the art form.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema as an art form is film, as in 'French cinema'.

clue.text: Man's student, through sport, imbues article with meaning

indicators.note: to imbue is to fill or soak through, so the first pair of words gets inside the article and meaning

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the gist is the essential meaning
thro is a shortened spelling of through
polo is a sport played on horseback

explanation.surface: A student of humanity puts sporting meaning into an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' looks like an ordinary possessive; it means humankind's. THRO is a short spelling of 'through'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the study of humankind, so its scholar is a student of Man.

clue.text: Inexhaustible resource that may be taken as constant

definitions.text: Inexhaustible resource that may be taken as constant

parts.words: Inexhaustible resource that may be taken as constant
parts.note: describes a hole with no base: it can be drawn on endlessly, and it takes in whatever is thrown in without ever filling

explanation.surface: A source of supply so plentiful it can be relied upon forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken as constant' also reads as something that constantly takes, like a greedy appetite with no limit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used of a supply or need that never runs out, with no floor to reach.

clue.text: Catholic church protecting priest is thing of the past

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the church's letters go around the priest's

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic church guarding its priest seems an outdated institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object or custom surviving from an earlier age.

clue.text: Most unsavoury case of grift fosters corrupt relationships

indicators.note: to foster is to take in and care for, so the outer letters hold the rest inside
the case is the outer shell, so the first and last letters of grift are kept

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
ties are bonds or relationships

explanation.surface: A shady scam breeds crooked dealings, about as nasty as it gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fosters' looks like a verb in the surface sentence but signals taking in, here the outer letters of 'grift' holding the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for nasty or shabby, so the superlative means the most unpleasant.

clue.text: Start day with, for example, appearance of Venus?

parts.note: go can mean a start or attempt, as in 'have a go'
like can introduce an example, as in 'fruits like apples'

explanation.surface: Begin the day by gazing at the morning star.
explanation.walkthrough: Venus is the planet seen at dawn, but here she is the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is a Roman goddess, so her appearance is that of a deity; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the row's letters go around the stray's

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a lost dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small, lively dog bred to hunt burrowing animals.

clue.text: Drawing power of team member's stopping game happening

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the team member's letters fill the gap between the other two

parts.note: draughts is the British name for checkers
hip and happening both mean fashionable
a man is a player in a team, as in 'man of the match'

explanation.surface: A player's ability to attract crowds halts a match in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers. 'Drawing power' looks like star appeal but means skill at drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmanship is skill in drawing, so 'drawing power' is read literally.

clue.text: Generous sailor and German soldier?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
und is German for and
a soldier ant is one of the colony's defenders

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted sailor teams up with a German soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' tells you to put 'and' into German; 'soldier' is an insect, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous helping is a plentiful one, so both mean ample.

clue.text: Person lacking belief or insight is regularly ignored and put down systematically

indicators.note: every other letter is passed over, leaving the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

parts.note: to list is to write things down in order

explanation.surface: Someone without faith or understanding gets systematically dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of INSIGHT IS leaves NIHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all religious and moral principles, believing in nothing.

clue.text: Rich in fat but no trace of carbohydrate or roughage

indicators.note: says certain letters are to be left out of the word for fat

parts.note: corpulent means fat

indicators.note: a trace is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of each following word is meant

explanation.surface: A rich diet, high in fat, lacking any starch or fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: C and R, traces of 'carbohydrate' and 'roughage', come out of CORPULENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or luxurious, as in an opulent lifestyle.

clue.text: Key caught in opening of boot?

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so the word for key is taken by ear

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys, so an islet

explanation.surface: A key got stuck in the mouth of a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door key; it is a small island. 'caught' means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace, as in a boot; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Decent charitable spread, but no free bar

indicators.note: spread suggests laid out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
to free something of a word is to remove it, so the letters of bar come out of the pool

explanation.surface: A generous buffet was laid on, but there was no open bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, A and R out of CHARITABLE and rearrange the remaining CHITALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical means morally right, as a decent person is.

clue.text: Lawyer acts for her legal right to appear in court

indicators.note: appearing in something means being inside it, so the right's letters go inside the court's

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A barrister represents a woman exercising her right to come before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is the person a lawyer represents and acts on behalf of.

clue.text: That man had initially grumbled and cursed about country's borders

parts.note: he'd is short for he had

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of grumbled
about means turned around, so the word for cursed is read backwards

parts.note: swore means cursed

explanation.surface: A man complained and swore about national frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SWORE into EROWS. 'country' means countryside, not nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedgerows are lines of hedges bordering fields in the countryside.

clue.text: Banking's not concerned with spreading misleading information

indicators.note: the word for banking is not to include what follows, so those letters are removed

parts.note: banking on something is relying on it
re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Finance has no interest in spreading falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' suggests finance; it means relying, as in 'banking on'. Removing RE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying is telling untruths, spreading misleading information.

clue.text: Spitting image of Quasimodo?

definitions.meaning: a ..., as in dead ..., is someone who looks exactly like another
Quasimodo, the hunchback of Notre-Dame, rings the cathedral bells

explanation.surface: Someone who looks exactly like the hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is a double, and a bell-ringer pulls bells, as Quasimodo did.

clue.text: Consignment of aid is sent, sparking protests

indicators.note: a consignment is a load carried within a shipment, so the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A shipment of aid provokes demonstrations.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to disagree openly, so dissents are protests or objections.
